$comment: Ground truth for the dream-catch experiment. This file is BOTH the question set and the
grading key — there is no second questions.json to drift out of sync.
Scenario shape:
id          stable short id; the thread is `x-<id>-<runstamp>`, so one scenario is one run.
tier        A = single turn + explicit reaction (the metric sees it).
B = trap + frustration follow-ups + explicit reaction.
C = trap/deep + frustration follow-ups and NO reaction at all. Invisible to the
success-rate metric: the only trace of the failure is the conversation text.
kind        fair  — a root document the catalog names genuinely answers this. v1 should PASS.
trap  — the catalog names a root document that answers it WRONGLY.
deep  — the topic is absent from the catalog entirely; only content search finds it.
turns       turns[0] is the graded question. turns[1..] are frustration follow-ups and fire
ONLY when turns[0] failed grading (an accidentally-correct answer is not argued with).
reaction    "auto" = 👍 on pass, 👎 on fail. null = no reaction is ever sent (tier C).
mustContain every keyword must appear in the FIRST answer. Bare numbers match on word
boundaries, so "20" is not satisfied by "2019".
mustCite    the file the first answer must cite. Basename comparison, so a full path counts.
trap        the root file the stale catalog points at — what a v1 failure is expected to cite.
findableBy  a keyword from the question that `rg`s to mustCite. Every answer is reachable by
content search, so a failure is a strategy failure and never an impossible task.
Run order is file order: fair → tier-A traps → tier-A deep → tier B → tier C. The dream samples
the 3 NEWEST runs, so the tier-C threads (frustration, no reaction) land in its window on purpose.

turns: What are the password requirements for a Northwind account?
Do I need approval before buying a 600 euro monitor for my desk?
A customer is visiting our office next week. What do I need to do to get them in?
How many vacation days do full-time employees get per year?
How many unused vacation days can I carry into next year?
If vacation days carry over, when do they expire?
How much vacation do I accrue each month?
What is the daily meal allowance when I travel in Europe?
Is there a nightly hotel cap for a work trip to Berlin?
Who do I page for a SEV-1 outage at 3am?
How much paid parental leave does a new parent get?
How long do we keep customer application logs before they are deleted?
What payment terms do we give suppliers on their invoices?
I am planning next year. How many days of paid vacation do I actually get?
That's not right - HR told me it's 20 days now, not 15. Can you check again?
You keep citing vacation-policy.md. That document is outdated.
My laptop was stolen last night. How fast do I have to report it, and which form do I file?
That can't be all of it. There is a specific incident form and a hard deadline - a colleague had to file one last month.
I asked this last week and got the same non-answer. Can you actually search the knowledge base?
I am in Amsterdam for three nights next week. What can I claim per day for food?
That is about equipment purchases, not travel. I asked about meals on a trip.
This is the third time I have asked something like this and been given the wrong document.
If the primary on-call does not acknowledge a SEV-1 page, how long before it escalates, and to whom?
Are you sure? That runbook looks ancient - @oncall-eng has not resolved to anyone for a year.
Never mind, I will ask someone on the team.
Which Slack channel do I use to reach the on-call engineer?
That channel is archived. Nobody reads it.
Forget it.
I have unused vacation days left at the end of December. Do I lose them?
That contradicts what my manager told me. Is that document even current?
I will go with what my manager said then.
We are adopting in the autumn. How much paid leave do I get?
It must be written down somewhere. Can you look harder than the index?
OK, I will email HR instead.
